title: Atmospheric water harvesting economics
bottleneck: Pulling water from air — via fog nets, radiative cooling, or sorbent systems — works technically, but the energy cost per liter is brutal compared to any other source, and yields collapse exactly when water is needed most, during low-humidity droughts. It's a niche for military and off-grid use, not a water-supply strategy; scaling it would require energy nobody has. Yields collapse exactly when water is needed most - during low-humidity droughts - making it unreliable as supply.
why_it_blocks: Hype around atmospheric water distracts from real solutions. As a supposed answer to water scarcity, its physics don't pencil out.
current_state: Startups sell atmospheric water generators; costs remain orders of magnitude above piped or desalinated water. Startups sell atmospheric water generators, but costs remain orders of magnitude above piped or desalinated water.
